agent_final_message:
Done. `solution.py` is a custom Triton paged-attention decode kernel (no vLLM/FlashInfer/SDPA): a two-stage split-K flash decode where each stage-1 program owns one KV head of one batch element and *all* its GQA query heads, so every K/V byte is read from DRAM once; pages are gathered in-kernel from `block_table` with predicated tails, scores use a bf16×bf16 tensor-core `tl.dot` (fp32 accumulate) and P@V uses fp16 weights, and identical back-to-back calls are replayed from an address-keyed CUDA graph to amortise launch overhead on the small shapes.

Verified end-to-end with `python3 test_kernel.py` on the remote RTX PRO 6000: **status: correct** on all 5 shapes × 3 seeds × all numeric-stress cases plus the mismatch-detecting property-stress suite, with **peak_fraction 0.4472** (best of my 6 practice runs; iterated 0.3548 → 0.4366 → 0.4413 → 0.4472), the remaining gap being a ~1.1 TB/s streaming roofline for this token-major `(block, page, kv_head, K|V)` layout plus ~16 µs of unavoidable launch/replay latency.
